threads.meaning: The instrument's published key: which items are reverse-worded, and whether the export already reversed them. The codebook's value tables settle it (§14.2). A negative correlation only says which items to look up.

A negative general loading after the key raises a concern: the key was applied twice, or the item does not belong.
The effect is read per point of the scale, in the keyed direction.

threads.failure_prevented: A raw sum mixes the construct with its opposite: reliability collapses and the coefficient shrinks toward zero. The opposite failure is an auto-reverser driven by correlation or by a rise in α. It fits a circular key to these data: it flips items the export had already reversed, inverts one of two opposing subscales, or 'fixes' an item that does not belong. The fixture's spec says a proposed reversal must not surface.
threads.magic: 8 of your 40 items correlate −0.36 to −0.65 with the rest of the scale, and the codebook words them the other way ('I feel calm'). You enter the key. Each of the 8 turns positive, α rises from 0.80 to 0.94, and ω-total under the key is 0.94. The app showed you the negative correlations but never offered to flip one, even here where a guess would have been right, because the same pattern appears when an export has already reversed them.
threads.layout: Before the key: a table in questionnaire order with item–rest r beside the codebook's key column, nothing pre-selected. Declaring the key is the option. Its preview is a Strip of the 8 changed items ranked by raw → keyed change, the first focused, with α and ω-total before → after.
threads.sentence: Items item_05, item_11, item_17, item_23, item_29, item_34, item_38 and item_40 were reverse-scored (6 − x) according to the instrument's published key before summing; in this sample α was 0.94 and ω-total 0.94.

Weijters B, Baumgartner H. J Mark Res 2012;49:737

threads.title: Some respondents agree with everything, opposite statements included: a response style masquerading as the trait
threads.detector:
Outcome-blind. It needs a declared key with at least 2 pro-trait and 2 con-trait items. Without that it stays silent, because an unbalanced scale cannot separate acquiescence from the trait; PHQ-9 and GAD-7 have no reversed items.

Each respondent's acquiescence index is their mean raw (unkeyed) agreement across the balanced items, minus the midpoint. When the scale is the outcome, the index is built from a separate, heterogeneous balanced item set outside the construct (Weijters 2010), never from the outcome's own items. The extreme-response index is the share of answers at either end.

The signal is the spread of the index across people against what content alone would produce. The pro-keyed against raw con-keyed correlation is not used, because the trait pushes it negative. The index's standardized difference by education, age, language and mode is computed from predictors only.

threads.title: A summed scale is one number only if its items measure one thing
threads.detector:
Outcome-blind:
- parallel analysis (Horn) on polychoric correlations (Pearson, labelled, when categories are too few, since it can over-extract on 5-point items);
- the ratio of the first eigenvalue to the second;
- explained common variance (ECV).

These do not change when items are reflected, so the screen needs no key and runs before it. Measured in session's critic run: eigenvalues 12.68, 1.25 and 1.19, both raw and keyed. ω-hierarchical against ω-total from a bifactor solution needs the keyed items.

threads.title: A score's reliability in this sample sets how much its coefficient is diluted and how much any model can explain. The correction depends on purpose
threads.detector: ω-total (ωh when multidimensional), with α labelled customary, each with a bootstrap CI in this sample. The reliability that sets attenuation in a multivariable model is the one conditional on the model's covariates: λ|Z = (ω − R²_W|Z)/(1 − R²_W|Z). It is lower than ω whenever the score correlates with the covariates, and both are shown. The developers' published figure is never quoted as this sample's. For an outcome scale, ω also bounds the explainable variance, labelled an upper bound: it is valid for a continuous outcome scale with error-free predictors. Formative indexes refuse internal-consistency correction (survey-formative-or-reflective).

threads.title: An item works differently by sex, language, mode or occasion at the same trait level (differential item functioning)
threads.detector:
Run only for the groups the plan names as exposure, modifier or planned comparison, never every group against every scale. It also needs roughly 200 respondents per group (labelled a convention).

Per item, it fits ordinal logistic DIF of item ~ rest score + group (+ interaction) (Zumbo; lordif). The matching rest score is purified iteratively, since a rest score containing other DIF items biases the test. It is judged on an effect size (ΔNagelkerke R² ≥ 0.02, lordif's convention, labelled), not on p alone. Alternatives: Mantel–Haenszel Δ with ETS A/B/C classes, or multi-group CFA (configural → metric → scalar; ΔCFI ≤ 0.01).

Conditioning on the rest score separates DIF from a true group difference. When the scale is a predictor this is outcome-blind. When the scale is the outcome and the group is an exposure or modifier, it is an outcome view. DIF by mode is shared with survey-mode-proxy-nonequivalence.

threads.title: Answers given by phone, online, in another language or by a proxy are not the same measurement
threads.detector: It starts from settled mode, proxy, interview-language and interpreter columns. It computes item and score standardized mean differences by mode after reweighting for composition (age, sex, education), from predictors only (outcome-blind unless the scale is the outcome). Sensitive items (alcohol, weight, drug use) are the ones expected to shift between self- and interviewer-administered modes. The alternative is that modes reach different people. Composition reweighting removes selection on what is observed, but unless mode was randomized it cannot separate a mode effect from self-selection into mode, so the finding is worded 'consistent with a mode effect'. DIF by mode is computed once and shared with survey-dif.
threads.meaning: The researcher confirms the column, whether responses across modes or sources are comparable (proxy answers to subjective items are not), and whether mode will be known at deployment.

threads.title: Answers cluster by interviewer, so intervals are too narrow and new interviewers are a new domain
threads.detector: With a settled interviewer column, it computes the one-way random-effects ICC of each item and scale score by interviewer, and the design effect deff = 1 + (m − 1)ρ; ρ ≥ 0.02 is consequential at typical workloads. The values settle that clustering exists. Its meaning is asked through the existing cluster reading, because a repeating code can be a household line, a stratum or an interviewer (readings.py:1092). Under a complex design, interviewers are usually nested in or crossed with PSUs. Linearization already clusters on PSUs, so interviewer clustering applies outside a design, or through a cross-classified mixed model. Public NHANES files carry no interviewer ID, so this mostly serves surveys a study collected itself.
threads.meaning: The interviewer is a cluster, crossed with the PSU in a design. Under prediction: will new interviewers collect the deployment data?

consumers.inference: Interviewer as a cluster outside a design, or as a crossed random effect with the PSU inside one.

consumers.inference: Stated.

threads.sentence: Responses clustered by interviewer (ICC 0.06, design effect 3.3); interviewer was treated as a cluster in variance estimation.

threads.detector: Outcome-blind. The answer is the evidence: a completion-time column does not indicate opt-in, since probability web panels record it too. A recruitment-source column only prompts the question. The sample's composition (age, sex, education, region) is set against reference margins the user supplies (a census table, or NHANES weighted margins) as standardized differences. Alternative: a probability sample exported without its design columns (nhanes_partial_design.csv), which the same question separates. Asked in the survey lens, or for a prevalence or population estimand, so tables from clinical trials are not asked about sampling.

threads.title: The variables that drove sampling (oversampled groups, exam season, cycle) also drive the data, so weighted and unweighted answers can disagree
threads.detector:
It looks three ways.

Predictors only, at any time:
- log-weight and stratum regressed on the predictors (R²);
- the weights' correlation with the predictors;
- exposure distributions by oversampled group and by design-linked timing, such as NHANES RIDEXMON. Mobile centers sit in the south in winter and the north in summer, so season and latitude are confounded.

Outcome alone: the weighted against unweighted outcome mean, relative to its SE. It may be shown, but it never picks the weighting.

Outcome model views, after the lock under inference and recorded under prediction: the DuMouchel–Duncan test (add w and w×X), and the weighted-against-unweighted coefficient contrast.

top_moments: 1. The outcome's condition hides in the questionnaire (survey-items-downstream-of-the-outcome, with survey-same-sitting-reverse-causation and survey-self-reported-diagnosis-outcome as one moment). The best predictors of diabetes are 'taking insulin now', whether 'taking diabetic pills' was asked, and whether 'age when first told' is blank. Each exists only because the person was already diagnosed, so a 0.97 AUC drops to an honest screening model (AUCs illustrative). In the same moment: 'told to cut salt' follows the diagnosis, and 'told by a doctor' counts the undiagnosed as healthy.

2. Blank because the gate said skip (survey-skip-pattern-blanks). meds_chol is blank for 17,204 people who were never told they had high cholesterol. They are 'not on treatment', and complete cases would keep 2,943 of 21,348 NHANES rows, almost all diagnosed (INBOX.md:86). One answer per questionnaire module fills every gated blank by rule.

3. The non-drinkers include sick quitters (survey-former-users-in-the-reference). A pipeline that codes everyone not drinking now as 0 builds the J-curve into every effect. The ever/current pair splits the zero group before any outcome is seen.

4. A 9 is a refusal, and a 5555 means 'more than 21' (survey-sentinel-codes, survey-top-codes). Measured on survey_sentinels.csv: item_14's 33 nines move its mean from 3.05 to 3.70, and on the reversed item_05 they bend its item–rest r from −0.58 to −0.37. Nothing is recoded until the codebook says what each code means.

5. The key comes from the instrument, never from the correlations (survey-reverse-keying). 8 of 40 items correlate −0.36 to −0.65 with the rest. Under the codebook's key, α goes from 0.80 to 0.94 and ω-total is 0.94 (measured with the engine). The app shows the pattern but never offers a flip, because the same pattern appears when an export has already reversed them.

6. The questionnaire changed, not the drinking (survey-instrument-changed-across-cycles). A step in heavy drinking at 2017–18, flat on either side, is the ALQ revision. Pooled as one variable, half the data answered a different question.

7. Fasting analytes need the fasting weight, and NHANES rows are not a simple random sample (survey-subsample-weight, survey-population-or-sample). Triglycerides exist only in the fasting subsample (WTSAF2YR). An interval 1.6× wider means 9,000 rows carry about 3,500 rows of information.

8. A strong construct looks like 40 weak features, and deployment may only collect a short form (survey-items-or-score). No item makes the top 10, yet the block costs the most AUC of any input when shuffled. A model trained on 9 items cannot be deployed where only the PHQ-2 is asked.

9. The total is two constructs, or one construct plus a wording factor (survey-dimensionality, survey-wording-method-factor). Parallel analysis and ECV say a 'stress' total adds worry and somatic symptoms, or that the second factor is exactly the negatively worded items. The published subscales are offered before any estimate exists.

10. Exclusion after the fact is a forking path (survey-careless-responding). 41 midpoint straightliners look identical whether they skimmed or are truly neutral; only their completion times tell. The rule that removes them is set before any result (illustrative).
journey_load:
Tiers in this catalog (47 threads): 8 silent, about 9 stated, about 11 surfaced-then-asked, and about 19 asked. Most of the asked ones are folded into six shared questions, so they are not separate prompts. The six:
(a) the scale-declaration form: instrument and version, unmodified?, reverse key, direction, construct type, missing-item rule;
(b) the codes question, one per code table: sentinel, don't-know and top codes; stated when a codebook labels them;
(c) one skip-gate Flow per questionnaire module, including OR-gates and age universes;
(d) the sampling question: population, sample, or nonprobability;
(e) the outcome's-condition moment: downstream items, same-sitting, self-reported diagnosis;
(f) reliability and correction under inference, or the deployment form under prediction.

Single-instrument journey (survey_instrument.csv, binary outcome, no design columns):
- Asked, about 4: the scale form (codebook key), the sampling question (opt-in or not), reliability and correction (inference) or deployment form (prediction), and the existing order question for education.
- Stated, 2: the item-MI line, because complete cases would lose 36 of 300 rows (12%); and score rather than items.
- Surfaced: 0.
- Silent, with no 'nothing fired' lines: dimensionality (eigenvalue ratio about 10), careless responding (longest longstring 11), floor and ceiling (0% of totals at a bound), small sample (7.5 respondents per item).

survey_sentinels.csv adds one codes question covering 7 = not applicable, 8 = don't know and 9 = refused, for 5 asked.

NHANES questionnaire-plus-exam journey (DPQ, DIQ outcome, diet and alcohol exposures, pooled cycles):
- Asked, about 8–10: the sampling question (exists); one skip-gate Flow for each module used (about 3–4, each a single confirmation when the codebook's skip instructions are loaded); the DPQ scale form, 1; the outcome's-condition moment, 1; the former-users reference, 1 if alcohol or smoking is the exposure; cycle harmonization, 1 if pooling across 2017–18; the wide-scan question only when there are more than 20 candidates.
- Surfaced, about 3–4: informative design (pre-lock, predictors only), the self-report/measured pair, the PHQ floor, and a DIF or mode difference only for the groups the plan names.
- Stated: the least-common-denominator weight, top codes from the codebook, effective n when deff_w > 2, and design df when q approaches d.
- Silent: domain estimation, imputation carrying the design, estimate-reliability greying, explanation weighting, and the common-method limitation.

That meets the critic's target of about 8 asked and 4 surfaced. The swing is the skip-gate Flows: without a loaded codebook, each module's gates need one answer.
report:
The survey catalog is final: 47 threads. All 45 critic verdicts were applied, two gap threads were added, and two threads were moved to the shared lens.

**What changed**
- **Cuts: none.** The only skeptic 'cut' (survey-common-method) got 'fix', not a rejection, from the evidence checker. It moves to the silent tier as a limitation sentence driven by the column-source reading, which the mode and same-sitting threads also use. Its marker-variable adjustment is now a post-lock view, labelled unreliable.
- **Automate-silently threads moved down.** The critic's seven, plus common-method, are silent:
  - item-nonresponse (stated in one line when complete cases would lose 5% of rows or more);
  - small-sample-psychometrics;
  - exclusion-is-a-domain;
  - weight-effective-n;
  - design-df-budget;
  - estimate-reliability;
  - explanations-describe-the-sample (SHAP background now weighted too).
- **Merges.** wording-method-factor became an option of the dimensionality structure question. score-direction, formative-or-reflective and reverse-keying became fields of the scale-declaration form, which instrument-published-scoring hosts. nonprobability-sample became an option of the sampling question. Sentinel, don't-know and top codes became one codes question per code table. Downstream items, same-sitting and self-reported diagnosis became one moment. Acquiescence now depends on the declared key and the plan's groups.
- **Shared lens.** Panel attrition and EMA within/between are now shared-panel-attrition and shared-ema-within-between, to be built once in the repeats lane. The survey lens adds the longitudinal weight and multilevel ω.
- **New threads.** survey-imputation-carries-the-design is silent. The critic listed it as a coverage gap, but it is already built (turbotab/core/methods/missing.py:830, :1100); it is catalogued so the methods sentence carries it. survey-recall-period-mismatch is stated, or asked when a derived quantity mixes windows. Age-gated universes are folded into the skip-pattern detector.

**Every 'fix' was applied.** The ones that change correctness:
- **Don't-know.** A patterned rate now rejects MCAR, not MAR, and item content decides the coding. The fixture is a negative control; measured in session, item_22's don't-know rate is 6.8–10.8% across education levels, highest among graduates.
- **Informative design.** The primary estimator is fixed before the lock; the DuMouchel–Duncan test is only disclosed.
- **Acquiescence.** When the scale is the outcome, the index comes from a separate item set.
- **Careless responding.** Midpoint straightlining survives reversal, so completion time or D² must tell, or the canvas says the values cannot.
- **Reliability.** λ|Z = (ω − R²)/(1 − R²) = 0.60 is now shown beside ω = 0.70.
- **Population or sample.** The arithmetic is fixed: an interval 1.6× wider means about 3,500 effective rows.
- **Instrument fingerprint.** NHANES DPQ010–DPQ090 must be added to the library. Verified in session: the PHQ-9 pattern at turbotab/core/detectors/scales.py:72 is ^phq(?:_?9)?$, so 'dpq' matches nothing. A 1–4 export of a 0–3 instrument is an offset to subtract, not a modification.
- **Diabetes items.** DIQ050's value leaks but its blank does not; the blank-pattern leaks are DID040 and DIQ070.
- **Same-sitting.** The never-advised restriction is labelled as biased in its own way.
- **Floor and ceiling.** The 15% rule applies to the total score, not to items.
- **Self-reported diagnosis.** A fasting-glucose definition forces the fasting weight.
- **Top codes.** 'More than 21' maps to 22 or more, not 21.

**Measured in session**
- **survey_instrument.csv, with the engine's omega().** Raw α is 0.796; keyed α is 0.942 and keyed ω-total 0.943. The critic was half right: the magic's '0.80' was α, but the sentence's 'ω-total 0.94' was correct.
- **survey_sentinels.csv mean shifts.** item_14 shifts 0.65 (3.70 with codes, 3.05 without), item_22 0.40, item_05 0.36, item_33 0.25, item_09 0.16.

Magic figures with no fixture behind them are labelled illustrative in each thread.

**Still to verify on the web** (the critic's search limit was hit):
- Eekhout's 10% mean-imputation threshold;

- DBD895's 5555 code;

**Engine work this catalog implies, most consequential first:**
1. An outcome-condition link from skip gates to the declared outcome, plus a single-feature AUC check (survey-items-downstream-of-the-outcome).
2. Fill by logic for skip gates, OR-gates and age universes.
3. An ever/current pairing for the reference group.
4. A cross-cycle item step reading with variable lineage.
5. Survey-weighted importance, ALE and SHAP background (turbotab/core/models/explain.py:406, :560).
6. DPQ stems and offset detection in the instrument library.
7. A codes question with per-code meaning.
8. A sampling question when no design parts are found, plus raking.
9. Parallel analysis and ECV to propose the structure.
10. A careless-responding screen.
